title: Large personal Amiga/CPC/DOS game and binary-document discovery
summary: Personally screen 863 candidate URLs and add 17 projects, with seven explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root personally searched 12 GitHub query routes, screened 863 unique URLs and inspected 24 pinned repository trees. Seventeen additions and seven explicit non-promotions. Original-source translations, binary document/language formats, partial semantic reconstruction, reused source lineages and instruction-graph execution are distinguished. No upstream game, compiler, installer, emulator or service was executed.

sources.reason: Layout-oriented assembly reconstruction gradually replaced by semantic C routines. Inspected spell-selection dialog using named structures and original UI functions, not instruction dispatch.

Recovers compiled Blitz Basic car physics, handling presets, collisions, AI paths and caravan towing, plus six-disk formats. Inspected explicit original 50 Hz rule interpretation and structured Rust vehicle state.
Static DSK recovery of two parts, 43 backgrounds, sprite/placement data and player mechanics. Inspected source-address jump/gravity findings and actual native enemy rules.
Implements WordPerfect binary writing from OpenDocument via librevenge events, filling historical reader-only compatibility gap. Inspected WP5 control generation and reverse-mapped character tables.
Reads WPG1/WPG2 record streams, bitmap compression, vector scenes and OLE-contained drawings; exports SVG/PNG. Inspected signed WP5 coordinate and record decoding.
Models document header, prefix packets and token stream including raw bytes and mapped functions. Inspected WPC header field decoding in addition to API wrapper.
Recovers DAAD databases and illustrations from disk/tape containers, inferring endianness and load bases from content. Inspected explicit condact catalogue and original compression/address evidence.
Reimplements original QuickBasic 4.5 engine in C with preserved graphics, sound and AdLib music. Inspected substantive game loop rather than an embedded QB/DOS executable.
Original QuickBasic source translated into TypeScript game systems, Canvas renderer and original resource parsers. Inspected explicit player collision behavior.
Reads and writes 0xFC QuickBASIC source files with hashed symbol references and reverse-Polish statements. Inspected structural reader and BASIC 7 PDS layout/type tests.
Recovers LN-signature help files from MASM, QuickBasic and related tools using Huffman and keyword dictionary decoding. Inspected header/topic mapping and text decoding implementation.
Semantic conversion of 2012 DOS QuickBasic game with original PCX/FNT/map formats and fixed-point physics. Inspected movement/collision implementation.
Rewrites original QuickBasic ENGINE.BAS into typed browser game systems. Inspected movement function referencing original source lines and exact 1/64-pixel convention.
Preserves original QuickBasic modules and adds semantic source merge/compatibility tooling for QB64 and FreeBASIC. Inspected merge logic and browser build compiling BASIC to C and WebAssembly.
Independently written C# engine consults released id source for rules and loads original maps/art/audio. Inspected difficulty-normalized actor marker implementation.
Browser engine with original-address-backed data/analysis and structured NPC conversation logic. Inspected stateful purchase/text effects, not an instruction dispatcher.
Restores and restructures historical C port of VMS Pascal Moria, including sources formerly supporting DOS/Amiga/ST. Inspected original-attributed store and bargaining logic.

Reviewed source explicitly credits Ben Baker Amiga and Zlatko Karakas DOS recovery, and README directs users to Baker official releases. Existing benbaker76/OpenSWOS and angree/openswos represent that lineage; separate original work not established here.
Game-agnostic reverse-engineering framework, with example scaffolds rather than a recovered named game/application. Relevant tool lead, outside this subject-focused batch.
Explicitly executes original 16-bit SmoothTalker under Unicorn with emulated Sound Blaster/DMA. Not a native recovered speech-engine implementation.
GodLib demonstrations and reconstructed visual effects, not a specific restored game/application. Keep as tooling/demo lead rather than padding this focused subject pass.
New QuickBasic paint application inspired by MS Paint. No original application source/data or reverse-engineered behavior established.
Experimental old Umoria snapshot; README directs users to Dungeons of Moria upstream. No distinct completed Atari restoration established from current tree.

Substantial recovery evidence, but inspected live decision subsystem decodes an address-indexed 8086 instruction graph with registers, flags and instruction dispatch. Retain for audit as game-specific emulation rather than promote as fully native recovered rules. Bounded seeded replay comparison does not remove this distinction.
